Most married women who are Alex Cooper's age (or mine) will tell you that they spent their 20s and often a good part of their 30s working, dating, having a good time, and becoming themselves, all of which put them in the position to become the person they wanted to be -- and meet the person they would eventually marry. Again, this is just like... how life has been for American women for a few decades now. We have not mostly married at 20 for a long long time.

This weird narrative has taken hold on the right that the left is selling "single, liberated womanhood" rather than.... feminists  actually just saying that women should have a variety of options and also shift and change as they wish. For the overwhelming majority of US women, life is first single and liberated, and then later married with children. This is normal and has been for many many years and I don't get why we're being weird about it.

I truly think we've made something special. So if this sounds like something you might like, I hope you take the leap and sign up. Full disclosure it's mostly women. Most come alone, some bring a friend. But you can come as you are, whoever you are, with whoever you want to come with.

Retreats are very very very fun and I hope you'll consider joining me! Not to toot my own horn too loudly but ever since my collaborator Emily and I hosted our first retreat together we've had multiple repeat retreaters return on every single retreat, and at this point we've done at least a dozen.

Imagine taking a week to have all of your needs met: someone offering you creative practice, someone offering you movement practice, dinner reservations made, interesting people around the table, wine poured on when you arrive. Space to make and move and be. onthegroundretreats.com/retreat/greece

I host writing and yoga retreats around the world. And no, "go on a yoga retreat" is not the answer to society-wide loneliness or burnout or any Big Huge Problems. But it is one way to give yourself a damn break. To have fun. To exhale. onthegroundretreats.com/retreat/greece

We hear a lot about loneliness epidemics, too much stress, too much time on screens, too little time with other people, too much work and not enough creation. One antidote: Travel to a magical place with a small group of people. Write. Move your body. Make lasting friendships.
